court: Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit

issues.label: PLRA exhaustion timing at original complaint
issues.why: Court must decide whether exhaustion is measured at the original complaint filing when Carter had not yet completed the grievance process.

issues.label: Amended complaint curing exhaustion defect
issues.why: Central question is whether an amended complaint filed after exhaustion cures a failure to exhaust at original filing.

issues.label: Weight of unpublished Hardin decision
issues.why: Court relied on non-precedential Hardin v. Hunt, whose persuasive authority and correctness must be assessed.

issues.label: Exhaustion as affirmative defense/proper vehicle
issues.why: Whether exhaustion is properly resolved on summary judgment before discovery and who bears the burden.

issues.label: Availability of grievance remedy
issues.why: Whether the grievance process was actually available given intake rejections, which affects whether exhaustion was required.

issues.label: Exhaustion of the reentry/reclassification informal complaint
issues.why: Carter never filed a regular grievance after Branch's rejection, raising whether that claim was exhausted at all.

issues.label: Intake rejection as proper exhaustion
issues.why: Whether grievances rejected at intake and affirmed on appeal count as exhausted or as procedural default.

issues.label: Separate exhaustion analysis for each claim
issues.why: First Amendment and Eighth Amendment claims may have different exhaustion timelines requiring individualized analysis.

issues.label: First Amendment retaliation elements against Branch
issues.why: Whether Carter plausibly alleged protected activity, adverse action, and causal connection.

issues.label: Whether informal complaint is protected activity
issues.why: Court must confirm that filing prison complaints/grievances constitutes protected First Amendment conduct.

issues.label: Retaliation claims against McCoy and Cabell
issues.why: Whether Branch's secondhand references sufficiently implicate the wardens' personal involvement.

issues.label: Supervisory liability standard for Clarke
issues.why: Whether Carter alleged Clarke's knowledge of and deliberate indifference to Carter's specific conditions.

issues.label: Section 1915A frivolity dismissal standard
issues.why: Whether the court properly applied screening standards in dismissing the Clarke claim.

issues.label: Eighth Amendment conditions-of-confinement merits
issues.why: Whether RHU conditions, analogous to Porter, plausibly state a constitutional violation.

issues.label: Effect of serious mental illness on Eighth Amendment
issues.why: Carter's mental illness may heighten the objective and subjective components of the conditions claim.

issues.label: Deliberate indifference/subjective component
issues.why: Whether defendants knew of and disregarded excessive risk to Carter's health from RHU conditions.

issues.label: Qualified immunity for individual defendants
issues.why: Whether the individual officials are entitled to qualified immunity, potentially unaddressed but relevant.

issues.label: Eleventh Amendment immunity of Commonwealth
issues.why: The Commonwealth of Virginia is not a proper Section 1983 defendant and may be immune from suit.

issues.label: Commonwealth as 'person' under Section 1983
issues.why: A State is not a 'person' subject to Section 1983 damages liability.

issues.label: Mootness of injunctive relief after transfer
issues.why: Carter's release from Sussex may moot claims for injunctive relief regarding those conditions.

issues.label: Pro se pleading liberal construction
issues.why: Court must construe Carter's filings liberally given his pro se status.

issues.label: Summary judgment before discovery propriety
issues.why: Whether granting summary judgment prior to any discovery was appropriate on disputed factual matters.

issues.label: Personal involvement of each defendant
issues.why: Section 1983 requires individualized showing of each defendant's participation in the alleged violations.

issues.label: Physical injury requirement under PLRA
issues.why: Section 1997e(e) may limit damages for mental/emotional injury absent physical injury.

issues.label: Scope of relief and filing fee assessment
issues.why: Court's IFP grant and fee assessment implicate PLRA cost provisions relevant to the proceedings.
